newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria restarts its oldest nuclear reactor.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria restarts its oldest nuclear reactor.

text.p: Bulgaria, urged by the international community to shut down its oldest nuclear reactor last May, began restarting it on Friday after tests showed it to be safe, plant officials said.
They said the Bulgarian Atomic Energy Committee had given the Kozloduy nuclear power plant's management permission to operate reactor number one.
Tests on the 440-megawatt reactor, which was built by Soviet engineers and came into operation in 1974, showed the metal of its pressure vessel to be safe and it can be operated.
Analyses of samples of the reactor's metal have been carried out by Germany's Siemens AG, Russia's Korchatov Institute and Bulgarian experts.

The European Union said in December the condition of the reactor vessel was within the limits of the acceptable safety level following the results of the tests, but appealed to Bulgaria to improve the safety of Kozloduy's oldest four 440-megawatt reactors and seek alternative energy resources.

The chairman of the Kozloduy plant Kiril Nikolov told Reuters that routine reconstruction of reactor number one had been carried out while it was idle. He said the reactor could be connected to the national power grid by Monday.
Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources, relies on the 3,760-megawatt Kozloduy plant for more than 40 percent of its power needs.
The plant, on the banks of the Danube, has four 440-megawatt reactors and two more modern 1,000-megawatt reactors. All are now operating, Nikolov said.
